page: Google Cloud Platform a3-edgegpu-8g is an accelerator-optimized bare-metal equivalent instance engineered for large-scale parallel processing. The server is equipped with 208 dedicated vCPUs spanning 104 physical cores based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8481C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz, accompanied by 105 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is provisioned at 1872 GB, providing 9 GB of RAM per physical core. Hardware acceleration is anchored by eight NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs offering a combined total of 640 GB of VRAM. Bundled storage consists of 6432 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD space.

Benchmark results demonstrate high multi-threaded compute and data pipeline capabilities. In multi-core tests, the platform recorded a stress-ng score of 167331.13 and a PassMark CPU score of 125152.39, placing it in the top tier of evaluated infrastructure. Extended instruction support is comprehensive, featuring hardware flags for AMX, AVX-512, and AVX-VNNI. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 431.78 GB/sec alongside 185.98 GB/sec in write throughput. In transaction processing and data retrieval, it registered 177.5 million Redis SET operations per second and top-decile scores in database operations.

The dense hardware configuration combines specialized matrix computing with large system memory and high-capacity NVMe scratch space. Single-core performance falls within median benchmarks, reflecting an architecture focused on parallel throughput across its 208 threads rather than isolated single-thread frequency. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included. The server is configured for deep learning training, massive AI model inference pipelines, high-performance computing simulations, and data-intensive distributed database workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform a3-edgegpu-8g is an accelerator-optimized server featuring 208 dedicated vCPUs on an Intel Xeon 8481C x86_64 architecture, 1872 GB of RAM, and 6432 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Acceleration is driven by eight NVIDIA H100 GPUs totaling 640 GB of VRAM. Empirical benchmarks show top-tier multi-threaded CPU output with a multi-core stress-ng rating of 167331.13, supported by Advanced Matrix Extensions and AVX-512 instructions. Memory bandwidth registers 431.78 GB/sec on uncached reads, while key-value store benchmarks demonstrate 177.5 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware resources favor parallel compute over individual core frequency, making the system appropriate for distributed deep learning training, massive language model inference, parallel data ingestion, and scientific simulation workloads.
